summary: Hans Krahe was a linguist who held posts at the University of Würzburg (~1936–1946), Heidelberg University (~1947–1950), and the University of Tübingen (~1950–1965).

Hans Küng worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University (~1948–1955), Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum (~1948–1955), and Catholic University of Paris (~1955–1956), later holding a post at the University of Tübingen (~1960–1996).

Hans T. Bakker, an Indologist and religious studies scholar, studied under Jacob Ensink (~1970–1984). He held posts at Utrecht University (~1988–1996) and the University of Groningen (~1996–2013), and served as a curator at the British Museum (2014).
Hans Urs von Balthasar, a scholar of philosophy and religious studies, studied at the University of Zurich (~1923–1928) and studied under Bernhard Geiger from 1924 to 1926.
Hans Windisch was a religious studies scholar who held posts at Leiden University (1914–1929), Kiel University (~1929–1935), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1935–1935).

Hans-Joachim Klimkeit worked in religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp (~1959–1963) and Gustav Mensching (~1963–1965), and became Direktor at the University of Bonn in 1972.
Hans-Werbin Köhler was an Indology scholar who studied under Eduard Hermann and completed his doctorate under Ernst Waldschmidt.
Hanung Kim is a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology. Kim earned a master's degree at Columbia University and a PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.
Har Dayal, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at the University of Delhi (~1901–1905) and SOAS University of London (~1927–1932).
Har Dutt Sharma was an Indologist who served as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of Delhi and held an affiliation attested at Hindu College, Delhi (1957).

Hara Prasad Sastri was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology scholar. He served as Principal at Sanskrit College and University (attested 1905) and Joint Philological Secretary at The Asiatic Society (attested 1905–1911).
Harabhatta Sastri was an Indology scholar who held posts attested in 1918 (as a pandit), 1922, and 1945 at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir.
Harabhatha Shastri was an Indology scholar who held a post at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, attested in 1911 and in 1916 as a Pandit.

Archaeologist Harald Hauptmann studied at Tübingen, Saarland, Heidelberg, and FU Berlin. His main posts included the German Archaeological Institute (1966–1971), Heidelberg Academy of Sciences (1989), Heidelberg University (1980–1994), and the German Archaeological Institute at Istanbul (1994–2001).

Harald Hundius, a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics, studied under Singkha Wannasai (~1971). He served as a lecturer at Chiang Mai University (1983) and was a professor at the University of Passau (~1993–2004).

Haraprasad Shastri studied at Presidency University, Sanskrit College, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. His posts included Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1900–1908), Sanskrit head at Presidency University (1895), and department head at University of Dhaka (1921–1924).

Hari Damodar Velankar was an Indologist who studied under Hari Mahadev Bhadkamkar. He held posts as Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai (attested 1944–1948) and Joint Director at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (attested 1959–1960).

Hari Shankar Prasad is a scholar in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University, under Ramakant Tripathi, and under doctoral supervisor Jan Willem de Jong (attested 1982).

Haridas Bhattacharyya studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta. In philosophy and religious studies, he held posts at Scottish Church College (1915), University of Calcutta (1917), University of Dhaka (1921), and Banaras Hindu University (1947).
Harish Chandra Mani Tripathi, an Indology scholar, studied under Karunapati Tripathi and served as Publication Officer at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1996).
